Text: In a Double-Checked Locking Singleton implementation, the reference variable must be declared {{c1::volatile}} to prevent {{c2::instruction reordering}} by the compiler/CPU during object creation.
Extra: Without volatile, the JVM can publish the object's reference address before executing the constructor, exposing a partially initialized object to other threads.

Text: The Bill Pugh Singleton pattern achieves lazy loading by encapsulating the instance inside a {{c1::nested static helper}} class, which is loaded only when getInstance() is invoked.
Extra: Since nested static classes are loaded lazily upon active reference, the outer class loading does not trigger instantiation.

Text: The Observer pattern defines a {{c1::one-to-many}} relationship between objects, utilizing an {{c2::interface}} to decouple the subject from concrete observer classes.
Extra: This allows any number of observers to subscribe or unsubscribe dynamically at runtime without affecting the subject class.

Text: The Factory Method pattern defers object instantiation decisions to subclasses by declaring an {{c1::abstract factory method}} signature inside the creator class.
Extra: This promotes creator-to-product polymorphism, as client code depends only on the abstract product type.

Text: The Builder pattern solves the {{c1::telescoping constructor}} anti-pattern, providing a {{c2::fluent API}} that constructs complex objects step-by-step.
Extra: Telescoping constructors lead to unreadable constructor chaining and high rates of parameter-ordering mistakes.

Text: The {{c1::Abstract Factory}} pattern is used to create families of related or dependent objects without specifying their concrete classes.
Extra: This pattern helps ensure that multiple related objects (such as Mac buttons and Mac scrollbars) are used consistently together.

Text: The Prototype design pattern relies on copying existing objects, which is often implemented in Java by overriding the {{c1::clone()}} method of the {{c2::Cloneable}} interface.
Extra: Cloneable is a marker interface. Overriding clone() allows making copies of configured objects instead of creating new instances from scratch.

Text: The {{c1::Adapter}} pattern uses {{c2::composition}} to wrap an incompatible class (adaptee) inside an adapter class that implements the target interface.
Extra: Java only supports single class inheritance, so the object adapter variant using composition is preferred over class adapters using inheritance.

Text: A Decorator class implements the same interface as the wrapped object and delegates calls to it, supporting recursive {{c1::decorator chaining}} to combine behaviors at runtime.
Extra: This provides a flexible runtime alternative to compile-time subclassing for adding features.

Text: In the Template Method pattern, the main skeleton method is declared {{c1::final}} to prevent subclasses from modifying the execution algorithm sequence.
Extra: Subclasses can only override abstract or hook methods called by the final template method.

Text: Modifying a Java collection structurally while iterating over it via an external iterator triggers a {{c1::ConcurrentModificationException}}, unless modified via {{c2::iterator.remove()}}.
Extra: This protects the iterator's state alignment against side-effects during traversal.

Text: A Repository acts as an in-memory collection of domain objects, working at the aggregate level, whereas a {{c1::DAO}} maps closely to low-level database table operations.
Extra: Repositories hide the persistence mechanism, allowing the domain model to remain database-agnostic.
